learning_outcomes.title: Interior and exterior angle reasoning
learning_outcomes.statement: a) Prove and use the Polygon Interior Angles Sum Theorem. b) Find and use the sum of exterior angles of a polygon.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: For a convex polygon, diagonals from one vertex form n − 2 triangles. Interior sum = (n − 2)180°. One exterior angle at each vertex, taken consistently around the polygon, sums to 360°.

questions.title: A • Build the theorem
questions.stem: Consider a convex polygon with n sides.

parts.prompt: Draw a hexagon. Triangulate it using diagonals from one vertex. Label the triangles.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: A correct convex hexagon has 3 noncrossing diagonals from one vertex, forming 4 triangles. Award 2.

parts.prompt: Use your diagram to explain why the interior angle sum of an n-gon is (n − 2)180°.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: An n-gon forms n−2 triangles. Their angles partition the polygon interior, so the total is (n−2)×180°. Award 3 for count, triangle sum, and conclusion.

parts.prompt: A regular polygon has each interior angle 156°. Set up an equation and find n.
Find its exterior angle and check the exterior angle sum.

questions.title: B • Exterior angles and algebra
questions.stem: A convex pentagon has one exterior angle at each vertex, all measured in the same direction. They are x°, (x + 10)°, (2x − 5)°, (x + 20)°, and (x + 5)°.

parts.prompt: Write an equation using the exterior-angle theorem.
Find all five exterior angles and the corresponding interior angles.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: Exterior angles are 55°,65°,105°,75°,60°. Corresponding interiors are 125°,115°,75°,105°,120°. Award 2 per correct list.

parts.prompt: Verify the interior-angle sum for the pentagon.

questions.title: C • Work backward and critique
questions.stem: A designer uses regular polygons in a tiled pattern.

parts.prompt: A regular polygon has exterior angle 18°. Find its number of sides.
Find its interior angle and total interior-angle sum.
A student claims a regular polygon can have each interior angle 145°. Test this claim.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: Its exterior angle would be 35°, giving n=360/35=72/7, which is not an integer. Such a regular polygon does not exist. Award 3.

parts.prompt: Explain why one exterior angle at each vertex of a convex polygon sums to 360°.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: Walking once around its boundary makes one complete turn. The consistent exterior turns sum to 360°. Award 2.
